tagline: Augusta's river road, named for Mary Ingles, who walked home.
intro: The byway is KY 8 through the city of Augusta, a trading post of 1786 on the south bank of the Ohio, where the highway becomes Fifth Street. Beyond town it keeps company with the river, southeast toward Maysville and northwest toward Cincinnati.

It is named for Mary Draper Ingles, taken by Shawnee raiders in the summer of 1755 and set to making salt at Big Bone Lick. That October she and another captive woman asked leave to gather wild grapes in the forest and kept going, following the rivers back to Virginia. Neither could swim. They crossed at least 145 creeks and rivers.

moments.title: Augusta
moments.text: Basil Duke's Confederates won a house-to-house fight here in 1862 but lost too many men to go on across the river into Ohio as planned.

moments.title: Augusta Ferry
moments.text: Running since 1797, when John Boude pushed it across by hand, the ferry is the only public crossing of the Ohio between Cincinnati and Maysville.

sources.label: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, Kentucky State and National Scenic Byways and Highways
